summary.headline: DBL Q1 FY27 standalone revenue Rs 1,930 crore and EBITDA margin 10.32%; consolidated PAT fell to Rs 128 crore from Rs 271 crore.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue was Rs 1,930 crore with EBITDA of Rs 199 crore (10.32% margin, up from 10.11%), and standalone PBT rose about 26% YoY to Rs 72 crore. Standalone PAT fell to Rs 39 crore from Rs 123 crore, but the base quarter included a Rs 98 crore divestment gain. Consolidated revenue dipped to Rs 2,378 crore from Rs 2,620 crore, with consolidated EBITDA of Rs 429 crore (18.05% margin). Management reiterated FY27 guidance (revenue growth 30-40%, EBITDA margin 10-12%, debt reduction Rs 600-800 crore) and announced a stake sale in under-construction transmission and solar projects (about Rs 8,400 crore project cost) to Alpha Alternatives.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: Completed three HAM packages worth Rs 1,700 crore on Bengaluru-Vijayawada Expressway (AP), all ahead of COD. Management says revenue from large new projects (transmission, roads, solar, water) has not yet started and will ramp from Q2-Q3.

segments.name: MDO (Mining)
segments.commentary: Q1 coal production 4.79 MT; MDO revenue about Rs 362 crore in the quarter per analyst calculation. Siarmal planned 27 MT and Pachhwara 7 MT for FY27; FY29 target 57 MT retained. Pottangi Bauxite production not yet started.

segments.name: Multi-asset platform (InvIT/HAM)
segments.commentary: Holds units worth about Rs 1,521 crore (Rs 1,314 crore Anantam Highway Trust plus Rs 207 crore Shrem InvIT). Next tranche of 11 HAM assets to be transferred to Anantam InvIT by March 2027, expected to yield about Rs 1,700-1,800 crore of units for <Rs 81 crore incremental equity.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin guidance of 10-12% (reconfirmed; analyst noted 11-12%).
Revenue growth guidance of 30-40% for FY27 reiterated; ramp-up expected from Q3, stronger in Q4 and into Q1 FY28.
Standalone debt reduction guidance of Rs 600-800 crore for FY27 reiterated; standalone net-debt-positive target by FY28 reaffirmed.
FY27 order inflow guidance of Rs 10,000-12,000 crore reiterated; bids worth Rs 15,000-20,000 crore pending opening.
Working capital days expected to reach about 120 by year-end and about 90 next year; from 131-133 days currently.
Finance cost for FY27 targeted at about Rs 350 crore.
Standalone capex guided at under Rs 100 crore for FY27, unchanged.
Coal production target of 57 MT by FY29; coal handling plant (CHP) expected to take about 1.5 years, with Siarmal at 27 MT (FY27), 35 MT (FY28), 50 MT after CHP.
capex_capacity: Siarmal total original capex Rs 2,730 crore, about 40-45% spent; more than 50% of equity already invested; around Rs 300 crore cash sitting at Siarmal SPV; Rs 235 crore residual equity to be funded from SPV accruals.
Siarmal debt sanction Rs 2,000 crore, Rs 60 crore drawn as of 30 June; around Rs 300 crore remaining to draw.

Transmission and solar stake sale to Alpha Alternatives: total equity requirement about Rs 1,600-1,650 crore; Alpha to co-invest 49% during construction; about Rs 900 crore structured equity already raised.

Anantam InvIT: 11 HAM assets, 4 to be flipped in August; 4 CODs done and 3 more by September; all 18 assets targeted for transfer by FY27 end or Q1 FY28, subject to NHAI NOC after six months of first annuity.
Other pipeline: 1977 MW solar mandate, Mekhali interstate transmission (Karnataka), water HAM, oil and gas portfolio to be considered for a future InvIT structure.
demand_pricing: NHAI FY27 pipeline: 54 highway/expressway projects, 2,442 km, about Rs 1.80 lakh crore (26 EPC, 21 HAM, 7 BOT). Awarding in Q1 was soft, particularly in national highways.
NHAI monetisation: 17 stretches (~1,693 km) targeted for FY27 via TOT/InvIT, expected proceeds Rs 30,000-35,000 crore.
Bid pipeline about Rs 1.5 lakh crore per Rohan; management later cited Rs 2.5-3 lakh crore across sectors, of which roads about Rs 1.25 lakh crore.
Declared L1 for Sikasar to Kodar Reservoir Link Canal Pipeline (Chhattisgarh), lump sum about Rs 2,524 crore.
Mining balance contract value about Rs 1.03 lakh crore; MDO reported order book about Rs 5,224 crore (3-year rolling).
Coal MDO pricing: Siarmal about Rs 550-600/t; Pachhwara about Rs 1,150-1,200/t; Siarmal coal fee currently 78%, moving to 100% after CHP.
Input costs: diesel bought at about Rs 140 and bitumen prices roughly doubled during the recent disruption; government reimburses 60-65% of fuel and bitumen cost increase.

qa_highlights.question: Will the FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 11-12% remain unchanged, and will revenue growth be back-ended?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 10-12% margin guidance is unchanged. Revenue ramp-up starts in Q3, steps up in Q4 and continues into Q1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How much bid value is pending opening, and what is the working capital outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 15,000-20,000 crore of bids are yet to be opened. Working capital days are expected to fall to about 120 by year-end and about 90 next year, from 131-133 days now.

qa_highlights.question: Can MDO revenue reach the Rs 2,500 crore FY27 level given Rs 362 crore in Q1 and 4.79 MT output?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said coal output is on track: 27 MT at Siarmal and 7 MT at Pachhwara in FY27, with Q1 low due to evacuation and a PSPCL strike at Pachhwara. Siarmal coal fee is 78% until the CHP is ready, rising to 100%, with a major revenue jump expected in FY29. Full-year math given as about Rs 600/t for Siarmal and Rs 1,200/t for Pachhwara.

qa_highlights.question: How will the Rs 1,700-1,800 crore of InvIT units from the 11-asset tranche be realised, and can standalone dividends help cut debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Four assets flip in August, with COD for four done and three more by September. All 18 assets are targeted for transfer by FY27-end or Q1 FY28, subject to NHAI NOC after six months of the first annuity. Siarmal equity will be funded from internal accruals, and the bank has permitted use of accruals within the project.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Alpha Alternatives deal equity split, and is DBL's share ~Rs 800 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Rohan said total equity is about Rs 1,600 crore, with Alpha co-investing 49% (about Rs 800 crore). The remaining about Rs 800 crore comes from DBL and structured equity, with about Rs 900 crore of structured equity already raised. Structured equity is to be flipped into InvIT units at COD.

qa_highlights.question: What is the consolidated net debt trajectory, and is there a consol-level target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no consolidated net debt target. The focus is on standalone net-debt-positive by FY28, while consolidated debt will cycle as assets are built and transferred to InvIT. Rs 7,801 crore consol net debt is referenced; the company cites Rs 45,000 crore of road HAM projects done.

qa_highlights.question: Other income breakup and standalone capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone other income was about Rs 40 crore: Rs 26 crore dividend from Alpha, about Rs 5 crore InvIT interest, and about Rs 9 crore FDR and other income. Standalone capex for FY27 stays under Rs 100 crore.

risks_watch: Revenue ramp-up depends on large projects (transmission, roads, solar, water, Bihar project, ERCP Rajasthan) starting in Q2-Q3; any slip threatens the 30-40% growth guidance.
Standalone net debt rose to Rs 2,106 crore from Rs 1,880 crore; delivery of Rs 600-800 crore debt reduction and standalone net-debt-positive by FY28 is critical.
MDO revenue run-rate: Q1 Rs 362 crore against a full-year need of about Rs 2,500 crore; Siarmal coal fee at 78% until CHP is completed (about 1.5 years).
Timing of Anantam InvIT transfers: NHAI NOC is required after six months of first annuity; any delay pushes InvIT unit receipts out, and management already cited a one-quarter slip in June.
Commodity and working capital pressure: diesel near Rs 140, bitumen prices roughly doubled; government reimburses only 60-65% of the fuel and bitumen cost increase.
Alpha Alternatives transaction: definitive agreements not yet signed, and structure/terms not disclosed; a separate call is promised.
Awarding was soft in Q1 with order inflow of only Rs 268 crore; FY27 order inflow guidance of Rs 10,000-12,000 crore needs large bid wins (Rs 15,000-20,000 crore pending opening).
Kerala (Wayanad) tunnel collapse: management attributes it to natural calamity; watch for any impact on tunnelling bids or project timelines.
key_quotes: So, none of our guidance that we had in the last quarter has changed and we are very positive around that.
Our goal to reach net debt positive on a standalone balance sheet by FY28 remains firmly on track.
Now, while our goals are twofold, we want to reduce debt on the standalone front.
So, in a sense, DBL balance sheet has free cash to reduce debt plus we have equity for our assets, where we build those assets and we get the upside of the higher valuation once the COD happens.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on guidance, saying none of the Q4 FY26 guidance has changed and that it will achieve the revenue, margin and debt targets. It was more cautious on Q1 specifics, citing soft awarding, elevated working capital and delayed MDO ramp-up, and deflected some detailed questions on the Alpha deal to a later call.

Pottangi Bauxite mining operations (not yet started)

Standalone capex guided under Rs 100 crore for FY27, mostly replacement; no big capex envisaged in Q1

growth.why: Management reiterated 30-40% FY27 revenue growth (midpoint 35%), but Q1 consolidated revenue fell to Rs 2,378 cr from Rs 2,620 cr, large new projects only ramp from Q2-Q3, Q1 order inflow was just Rs 268 cr against Rs 10,000-12,000 cr guidance, and NHAI awarding was soft.
